stem: A client has thirst, dry mucous membranes, and urine that is more concentrated than expected with an elevated urine specific gravity. Which interpretation best fits these findings?

options.A: The findings are consistent with body-water loss and concentrated urine, although urine specific gravity alone cannot establish the cause of the fluid deficit.
options.B: The findings are most consistent with marked fluid overload because concentrated urine and dry mucous membranes usually occur with excess volume.
options.C: The findings specifically diagnose diabetes insipidus because that disorder characteristically produces highly concentrated urine during water loss.
options.D: The findings represent a normal hydration pattern that needs no further assessment because elevated urine specific gravity is expected in euvolemic adults.

rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories states that urine specific gravity estimates urine concentration and that high specific gravity can occur with excessive water loss, including from sweating, fever, vomiting, or diarrhea. Low specific gravity may occur with diabetes insipidus. Combined with thirst and dry mucous membranes, the concentrated urine is therefore consistent with body-water loss, but specific gravity alone does not identify the cause. A is correct; B, C, and D conflict with the laboratory interpretation.
educational_objective: Interpret elevated urine specific gravity as concentrated urine that can accompany body-water loss while avoiding diagnosis from urine specific gravity alone.
source_version_date: Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories test catalog, rechecked 2026-08-16
source_claim_supported: Urine specific gravity estimates urine concentration; high SG may occur with excessive water loss; low SG may occur with diabetes insipidus; SG is a partial assessment and requires clinical context.

source_original.stem: A client has thirst, dry mucous membranes, and urine that is more concentrated than expected with an elevated urine specific gravity. Which interpretation best fits these findings?

options.A: The findings are consistent with dehydration and concentrated urine, although urine specific gravity alone cannot establish the cause of the fluid deficit.
options.B: The findings are most consistent with marked fluid overload because concentrated urine and dry mucous membranes usually occur with excess volume.
options.C: The findings specifically diagnose diabetes insipidus because that disorder characteristically produces highly concentrated urine during water loss.
options.D: The findings represent a normal hydration pattern that needs no further assessment because elevated urine specific gravity is expected in euvolemic adults.

source_original.rationale: An elevated urine specific gravity indicates relatively concentrated urine and can occur with body-water loss. Combined with thirst and dry mucous membranes, the finding is consistent with dehydration, but urine specific gravity alone does not establish the cause or a complete diagnosis. Diabetes insipidus characteristically produces dilute rather than highly concentrated urine.
source_original.source_detail: Clinical Information/Interpretation: increased urine specific gravity can occur with excessive body-water loss; decreased specific gravity can occur with diabetes insipidus. Interpret the result with clinical context rather than as a stand-alone diagnosis. Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories test catalog entry; live reference rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Reduction of Risk Potential: diagnostic tests, laboratory values, vital-sign monitoring and potential complications. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained key but replaced the broader diagnostic word 'dehydration' in the answer with the directly supported description 'body-water loss and concentrated urine,' preserving the clinical findings while avoiding diagnosis from SG alone.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Urine specific gravity and fluid-status interpretation
audit_findings.claim_audit: High SG/body-water loss and low SG/DI are direct Mayo interpretations; no stand-alone diagnosis is asserted.

distractor_audit.B: Contradicts dry findings and is not supported by the pattern.
distractor_audit.C: DI is associated with low SG.
distractor_audit.D: Elevated SG with symptoms is not simply normal hydration.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A fits both lab and clinical findings.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Reduced diagnostic overstatement and confirmed no unresolved precision.
